title: Memphis City Council devolves into chaos after data center moratorium vote postponed
key_facts: The Memphis City Council postponed a vote on a proposed year-long moratorium on new data centres at its meeting on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026.
Seven council members voted to delay the vote until 20 Oct, while five opposed the delay; one member was absent.
The proposed ordinance would pause new data centre projects for 12 months while the city studies their effects on health and on Memphis's power, water and other infrastructure.
Protesters chanted inside City Hall, police cleared the chamber, and a fight broke out in the lobby; police said no one was detained or injured.
Councilman J.B. Smiley Jr., the lead sponsor of the proposal (Memphis City Council), had pushed for a final vote on Tuesday.
Councilman Jeff Warren (Memphis City Council), who opposes the moratorium, warned that a year-long pause could push companies to build outside Memphis, to nearby counties.
Memphis Mayor Paul Young (city of Memphis) called for more rules on data centres while also pointing to the tax revenue they generate.
SpaceXAI runs the Colossus supercomputer facilities in the Memphis area, and some residents have raised concerns about power, water, air quality and noise.
quote_evidence: A Memphis City Council meeting descended into chaos Tuesday night after lawmakers postponed a vote on a proposed yearlong moratorium on new data centers, as protesters chanted inside City Hall, police cleared the chamber and a fight broke out in the lobby.
"If we pass a moratorium, there’s no reason for them to think they need to come here," Warren said, according to WREG.
The council voted 7-5 to delay the moratorium vote until Oct. 20.
why_it_matters_hint: A local vote on a 12-month pause on new data centres in Memphis, where a major AI computing site already operates.
